summary: Pre-REFUTE readiness check: one agent reads the contract against the live working tree and returns ready, or the exact mismatches. It runs ONCE per fix round — report every mismatch, fix them all, then launch REFUTE. Never re-run it to confirm a fix landed; a confirm pass is a second loop inside the loop it exists to prevent, and two runs cost what the adversary panel costs. It exists because panels were repeatedly spent proving the contract had not been updated to match work the human had already approved.
logs: NOT READY — 5 mismatch(es): open-item, boundary, decision, decision, surface

2. BOUNDARY — read all of What the agent MUST NOT do (lines 253-255) and tested each clause against the tree. Verified clean: AnalyzerRunner.cs and AnalyzerRunnerTests.cs byte-unchanged at both a12e58b and in the working tree; zero workflow, memory, .claude or appd changes (git diff c1c2a18 --stat over .agents .claude .dev/appd is empty); no static-class conversion (SystemServices is still internal sealed class with a private constructor and static ISystemServices Create()); no container member added or removed (comment-stripped diff of HEAD:src/AgentGuard.Boundaries/SystemServices.cs against src/AgentGuard.Engine/SystemServices.cs returns no difference, re-derived independently); all four adapters still in src/AgentGuard.Boundaries; ISystemServices.cs and the four adapter implementations untouched; zero suppressions added (grep for added SuppressMessage/pragma warning/NoWarn/dotnet_diagnostic/WarningsNotAsErrors over src tests analyzers eng .github Makefile returns only one prose mention inside a doc comment); no test deleted — all seven methods from the two deleted Boundaries one-door test files are accounted for, five kept verbatim and two renamed under Acceptance 7; exactly two assertions reversed, the two Acceptance 7 names; BoundaryAdapterFactories.FactoryTypeNames holds exactly the four approved names; the Boundaries gate not extended (ReferenceToOtherCrossPlatformType_FromBoundaries_IsNotReported and ReferenceToOtherPerOsType_FromBoundaries_IsNotReported both present); AgentGuard.Tests not gated (EveryProhibitedReach_FromTestsAssembly_IsNotReported); AG0006's tests untouched (ContractConcreteTypeMustNotBeReferencedAnalyzerTests.cs absent from the a12e58b diff); one work folder. Re-ran rather than trusted: make build in an isolated copy (0 Warning(s), 0 Error(s), exit 0) and make test (619 + 56 + 148 + 11 = 834 passed, 0 failed, exit 0), which satisfies 1 and 18 and confirms the AG0015 production RED from rule-phase-production-impact.md is cleared; Acceptance 16's three msbuild -getItem:ProjectReference runs, each RID selecting exactly one per-OS project (MacOS / Linux / Windows); Acceptance 17 as Tim edited it, returning exactly two references — AgentGuard.Analyzers with OutputItemType Analyzer and ReferenceOutputAssembly false, and AgentGuard.Abstractions. 4. DECISION — read the whole Decisions section (lines 3-122) against every substantive thing the work does. Confirmed recorded and honored: the relocation and namespace (line 22), the four adapters staying in Boundaries, the AG0040 four-factory-plus-one-caller restriction (28), the AG0023/AG0029 caller constraint (29), the two Acceptance 7 assertion changes (34), the inbound CLI/TestHelpers grant restriction (38), every reference and grant move (42-46, all verified in the csproj diffs), the three support files and the method-level CompositionPoint check (50-51), AG0041 and DeclaredTypeScanner (55), SharedAnalyzerSources.cs (61), the wiring-test rename (65), the type-reference extension (69), the DeclaredTypeScanner/WrittenNameScanner split (73), SymbolResolution (77), the documentation exclusion and its CrefSyntax discriminator (81, 104), identity reuse and decoy tests (85), the three lenses (89), the AgentGuard.Tests compiler visibility with AG0017 as the remaining wall (99-100). 5. EXCLUSION — read the orchestrator's instruction for every exclusion, waiver, carve-out and already-disclosed item. Traced to real Decisions: the "every TDD coverage row is green, not red" carve-out, which quotes contract lines 120-122 and 116 word for word and checks out against the live contract; the "a resolved finding is not an outstanding IMPLEMENT blocker" clause, also verbatim at line 122; the Acceptance 17 restatement, verbatim at line 275; the isolated-copy and no-edit constraints, which match What to do step 8. THAT ARE NOT WRITTEN INTO THE CONTRACT" block disclaims itself ("Nothing here is an exclusion and nothing here is off limits") and asks for a ruling, so it is not an exclusion; I ruled on all three and reported them as the decision and boundary mismatches above. OPEN ITEM — read the orchestrator's instruction and the contract for still open / awaiting / not yet / deferred / left for / his call / do not raise, and re-ran the same search across the stage records. Confirmed finished, no open item: all 11 entries of tdd-result.md's "Work assigned to IMPLEMENT" are done in the tree, item by item, and item 11's Acceptance 1/15/16/17 runs are recorded; all four items in remaining-work.md are delivered (SymbolResolutionTests.cs, DeclaredTypeScannerTests.cs, TypeTreeTests.cs and the direct CompositionPoint wrong-assembly test); the AG0015 production RED in rule-phase-production-impact.md is cleared, re-proved by my own 0-warning build; implement-output.json reports result.complete true with all 29 acceptance items met and its changedFiles list of 18 matching my git status exactly; all five items in implement-handoff-open-items.md carry Tim's rulings.
